Title: Black Mamba
Author: William  Friend
My Review:
3.5 stars for the story, that extra 0.5 for the good writing.

When I saw the book, I was fascinated by the cover because it seemed very cool. I was even more intrigued by the plot, so I had to claim it in Readers First.
After a bit of a struggle of getting it out of my post box, I started reading it immediately.
The book itself is not very scary or horrifying, but disturbing because you are not quite sure what the hell is happening, but want to know what happens next. This book made me feel the same as when I watched those speculative documentaries on children who had memories "from their past lives", a bit troubled by the story but curious.
Other than book a good horror book, it looked at grief and how families deal with it, which is essentially what Black Mamba is based on. There is a lot that plays in the story and you are given quite some detail about it, but more in depth into Pippa and Julia's childhood would complete the story even more.
I was expecting this book to have some odd supernatural things, but it did leave you with a sense of the story not being done, and the interpretation is quite open. Maybe a sequel?

I enjoyed this book quite a lot and it was a quick read. Also gorgeous, gorgeous cover

Title: Stone Blind
Author: Natalie Haynes
My Review:
I love Greek Mythology and I have been enjoying the more modern retellings of them, especially when they are from the point of view of what I consider the forgotten characters of a myth: the monsters, the servants, the crews, the spouses and children.
Medusa is obviously one of the forgotten: blamed for what happened to her, who made Perseus the hero he was, for slaying a Gorgon in her sleep.
'Stone Blind' is written in an accessible and direct language: mythology and classics retellings tend to feel at times extravagant and pretentious in their language and vocabulary, and that can be off-putting.
Natalie Hayes makes classical literature easily accessible and enjoyable to read.

I particularly enjoyed the chapters from the point of view of Medusa's head after she was decapitated, her perspective on the events presents an apathy that only a wronged person who can only resign to their fate has. It shines a whole new different light on the myth of Perseus.

I read someone else's review that said that this is "the story of Medusa" rather than Medusa's story and I quite agree because the narrative of the book follows the events leading up to the myth of Perseus slaying Medusa, carefully threading the stories of all the mortals, creatures and Gods that were part of Medusas' tragedy.
I would dare say it was a dominoes of events that led to the classic story of Medusa most widely known.

I also enjoyed the perspective of Medusa's snakes before her death, as it is a point of view no one ever really thinks about, and it shows how every part of us is affected by an event. I think it also illustrated how people can feel guilt about what happened to them, diving into all the what-ifs, when the blame belongs to everyone else but them.

I found this book so captivating I finished it in 2 days - thank you Natalie Hayes for getting me out of that book funk!

Title: Foster
Author: Claire Keegan
My Review:
"A good woman can look far down the line and smell what’s coming before a man even gets a sniff of it."

"You don’t ever have to say anything,’ he says. ‘Always remember that as a thing you need never do. Many’s the man lost much just because he missed a perfect opportunity to say nothing"

Two beautiful quotes from this short story. I quite enjoyed this book and the story it told. It's the reality of a lot of children in foster care, across the decades.
Through the writing style, you can definitely feel the protagonist is a child with a sense of responsibility and maturity acquired from having to take care of her siblings, from having had to grow up faster than her peers.
The open ending of the story leaves to wonder if the story could take a more chilling and eerie ending, or a sad and melancholy ending.
In a few short pages, Keegan created characters that are slowly being zoomed in on, starting from the general idea of them being good foster parents, to then uncovering their history, peeling back each layer as the story progresses.

A great, enjoyable story.

The characters are well written, and I like that the protagonist has her own garden and that people consult her for medicines and general health care.

My Review:
This book pleasantly surprised me. The premise of the book was very interesting and I was excited to read it when I saw it on Readers First. The book started quite in an interesting manner, and I started to feel defeated when I learnt that Kitty was an influencer, making the book slightly repulsive (to me at least). But then things took for the worse in the book, but for the better for me because I absolutely loved it! Other than being greatly enjoyable, it is a really powerful commentary on the #MeToo movement, on femicide, on domestic abuse, on toxic masculinity. 'How to kill men and get away with it' is a greatly enjoyable book, with a powerful message.
I must say if gore, blood and explicit violence is not for you, read with discretion because some parts are very graphic.
Beautiful cover also.

PS: I give the book a total of 5 stars because I wasn't too satisfied with the ending, but bonus star for the looks old men gave me on the train when I was reading the book. Nothing is more satisfying than seeing an old man stare at you, then sitting down opposite him and open this book so he can read the title.

Title: This Is How You Fall in Love
Author: Anika Hussain
My Review:
Honestly I was not expecting to love this book so much! I am not a big fan of romance and I only usually read it on holiday on the beach because they are sweet, quick reads. However this book had me gripped and out of my reading slump. I love the friends-to-lovers trope, and the fake dating sounds exciting, but what I love even more is choosing yourself first, and this book did it brilliantly.
Not only does it have great representation all around, but it is fun, sweet and honestly relatable.
The friendship between Adnan and Zara was wonderfully built, to the point I ached for a friendship like that with family friends that hang out together like their families do. This book also goes beyond and talks about familial relationships and communication and touches over the different types of love.
I loved the ending and the idea behind the documentary! Cover majestic as usual.
Really loved this book, and will definitely read more by the same author.

Title: The Sharp Edge of Silence
Author: Cameron Kelly Rosenblum
My Review: Honestly this book surprised me: I. ate. it. up. I had not read a book so fast in forever, and it made my commute fly because of how engrossed I was in this. This book has a great insight into the unfortunate reality of elite and private schools, where bad things that happen tend to be swept under the rug, as to not tarnish the reputation of the school. But things such as these need to be spoken out loud, screamed at the top of the lungs until the attacker feels the consequences of their own action. I think this book showed how quickly girls who are not even very close will immediately group together to protect each other, and the female rage in this book satiated me all right. Mind the themes, as it can be quite heavy in certain chapters, as this topic is a difficult one. I think the author captured teenage experiences in a quite realistic way, and also the rage Quinn feels. I appreciate the author showing the girls walking away from toxic situations and relationships, which lately seems to be too romanticised in books ( Colee.. ahem anyway). A strong and powerful story. And the cover: wonderful! I love the " boys will be held accountable" written in pink.

I would say this book is 3.5 stars. It was quite good to be fair, and the plot twist was quite unexpected, well thought out, as well as described and carried out.

Overall, well written book and an enjoyable story. Also, great cover!

It was nice to have the insights of somebody who actually went through what is talked about in the book, like panic attacks. I personally never experienced panic attacks or irritable bowel syndrome (can't remember the complete name) but in case it happens to me or to somebody in the future I might be more helpful than just standing on the side like a fish stick.

I can definitely see the author worked at BuzzFeed 'cause their typical humour kinda stuck with her. But hey it wasn't completely unpleasant.

The little questions at the end were quite good, even though I didn't really apply myself to answer them, but just quickly read them. I think this makes a quite good workbook.

Overall this book was quite good, and contextualising things like anxiety and other mental health issue by drawing advice from first-hand experience gave a more raw and personal touch to this book. Greatly recommend!

Title: The 4-Hour Body: An Uncommon Guide to Rapid Fat-Loss, Incredible Sex, and Becoming Superhuman
Author: Timothy Ferriss
My Review:
I have heard great things about this author, and I had a free credit on audible so I thought I would try this book.

*This is just my opinion. Read it if you are interested or skip it. I really don't care but I just needed to get this out of my system.

At first I was intrigued: the book promised to develop the body of a superhuman with minimal but effective effort. Enticing no?
BUT it was a WHOLE load of absolute crap. Yep, I was disappointed too (It's my personal opinion, everyone has their own perception and this is mine).

Initially, I was like " hmm let's hear this. He experimented on himself, cool." Then it said that you should only eat fruit once a week, have a huge cheat day where you almost make yourself sick (and sh*t it out as quickly as possible), and eat a lot of legumes and beans. I swear to whatever deity is up there that, if I rock up to a guy's house and open cabinets, and I see an absurd amount of cans of beans, I will adopt a cat for every can this mf bought.
Just imagine somebody doing this nutrition plan at the supermarket: they would look like those people who build bunkers in their basements to survive whatever cruelty/menace humanity is working on in the moment.
If this wasn't absurd enough, the author discussed how actually reducing your workouts might make you build more muscle instead. Some things were sound, some others weren't (you telling me lifting dumbbells and doing air squats gives you a six pack??), or WILLINGLY subject yourself to ice cold showers and baths. Humans didn't work hard to build entire water systems and pipes for us to bathe like a penguin in the Artic.

And the cherry on top (erhm) was the sex chapter. I was like "wtf is this?!". I am not an expert so I can't verify this information, but I am pretty sure I would feel dehumanised if a guy I hooked up with used the opportunity for me to be a lab rat for his experiment. Hopefully the women were aware and for their sake I hope what the book is preaching is true. This chapter taught me more maths and geometry than my math GCSE.

I researched people who allegedly followed this diet, and there are some mixed results out there. I was curious to see if someone out of his test subjects had tried it, and what the results were.
I would be interested to hear doctors and specialists comment on this to see what they think is healthy and what is bs.
Something about this book does not sound healthy at all, and actually ranges on borderline unhinged, but eh to each their own.

**Gotta add that I find it interesting that, while reading the reviews here, I noticed how the majority of men gave this book a high ratings, while women tend to give a lower one. Interesting...

Title: The 5 AM Club: Own Your Morning. Elevate Your Life
Author: Robin Sharma
My Review:
*3.5 stars rounded down.
Ok this book was interesting, both in the good and bad way. I want to talk about more what implementing what the book mentions feels like.

What Sharma is preaching about the benefits of waking up at 5 AM sounds kind of sensible, but I would not believe it until I tried it myself.
After I read the book, I woke up at 5AM religiously and followed a similar routine to what the book advised, adapting it to my needs and school schedule. I felt good at the beginning, but after a month and a half I dreaded the sound of the alarm at 4:55 AM.
I would feel tired at around 3 pm, which is not ideal when your lessons finish at 5, and you need to do homework at night.
I did enjoy the calmness with which my mornings started: taking a walk after waking up and dedicating an hour to myself to read and reflect was enjoyable and it made me feel mentally better. I didn't find sustainable for myself, but you gotta try it out before deciding if it works for you.
But waking up at 5 AM is not for everyone, and the proposed routine does not work when your schedule is decided by somebody else (i.e. school, university or a job). I guess it would work for freelancers and entrepreneurs or something, but it is hard. I did in summer and I was struggling: I can't imagine waking up so early in winter, especially in the UK when the sun comes out at 7 am in the winter months.

Anyway, you can be productive regardless of the time you wake up, but I definitely recommend taking the first hour of your day to dedicate to yourself however you want (you don't need to exercise or journal) to start the day right, and giving yourself about an hour to unwind at the end of the day.

Title: A Level Chemistry for OCR A Student Book

My Review:
Took me almost two years to read this book because of how content-heavy it is. Oddly enough, they put the definitions at the end of the topic in the glossary, part of the book that 1/10 student knows about, and not in the actual relevant page.
Also very heavy to carry: I don't know if at this point I have scoliosis or strong back muscles, but one thing I have gained for sure is trauma and hate for colours.

My Review:
*Note: I was given an ARC for an honest review

This book has been sitting in my Goodreads TBR for too long, so when I saw the opportunity to get an ARC I jumped.

Wicked Academia is a very well written fantasy book, with well-written characters.

I liked how it slowly built up to the triplets going to the Celestial Academy, and didn't rush into it, like many other fantasy books.
This created a good atmosphere and you really get to know the characters.
The triplets are each so unique and different, completing each other. Marion is a traumatised, sweet girl who takes a lot of responsibility, Vivian is sweet and romantic, and Timothee deserves to be wrapped in a blanket because he is stepped on too much.
I am not a fan of a romance, love at first sight and all that, but I am lenient towards the enemies to lovers/love hate trope, like Khalid and Marion's relationship. They have me rooting for them like British lads at Wembley, and THAT ONE SCENE! I was reading it on the Underground and my face went like :-O.
Darius and Vivian are so pure and cute, and it's easy to see where their dynamic is going.

I thought the book was going to continue past the Star Ceremony (which held me on edge till all of them swallowed their stars) and I want more: I am glad the sequel is being released soon.

Well executed world, well built relationships and friends, and well thought of magic. I can see the world and the society was thoroughly planned to the smallest details, and so were the characters.

In the future sequels I would like to read more of the original story of the Gods, and about the triplets' father/kidnapper??

I enjoyed this very much and I am excited for the sequels. 10/10

Title: Poisoned

My Review:
I absolutely loved this retelling of Snow White!
I adored how Jennifer Donnelly stuck to the quite gruesome Grimms' brothers fairy tale and made it about a strong, compassionate, fearless and kind woman, who fights for her throne back and is not awakened by Prince Charming passing by.
I am thrilled by the ending, which left me wondering whether or not there are going to be more books based on fairy tales retellings, and I shall expect so.
Jennifer Donnelly wonderfully captivating and fast-paced writing brings you directly into the story and plays it out in front of you like a scene from a film or a play in the theatre. Sometimes, it really feels like a story from a history textbook that we learn at some point in life.
Snow White has always been one of my least favourite princesses, however, 'Poisoned' by Jennifer Donnelly made me like her much more.
